title: Molina's account of the nature of grace: illumination and motions
source_text: XCIII. Quae sit autem natura divinae illius gratiae, quae diverso respectu praeveniens & cooperans est, & quam liberum hominis arbitrium efficacem vel inefficacem reddit, prolixe explicat Molina disputatione 45. ad articulum 13. quaestionis 14. Et primo quidem in genere gratiam illam constituit in mentis quadam illuminatione, & in motibus quibusdam voluntatis.
pass_a_gloss: XCIII. But what the nature of that divine grace is, which in different respect is prevenient & cooperating, & which the free choice of man renders efficacious or inefficacious, Molina explains at length in disputation 45. on article 13. of question 14. And first indeed in general he places that grace in a certain illumination of the mind, & in certain motions of the will.
pass_b_english: Thesis XCIII. Molina explains at length, in disputation 45 on article 13 of question 14, the nature of this divine grace, which is prevenient in one respect and cooperating in another, and which man's free choice makes efficacious or inefficacious. To begin with, he places that grace in general in an illumination of the mind and in certain motions of the will.

lemmas.gloss: in different respect prevenient and cooperating
in a certain illumination of the mind

choices.why: Molina places the first part of prevenient grace in knowledge helped by God's special influence.

bible_refs: Luis de Molina SJ, Concordia liberi arbitrii cum gratiae donis (Lisbon, 1588), question 14, article 13, disputation 45.
